# Morrow | Two-core codimension-two winding gate (SANDBOXED, 2026-10-13)

**Question.** Does a closed codimension-two defect generated by intersecting two impenetrable finite-core boundaries support *accessible* winding-one loops? This extends Morrow/Kestrel's 2026-10-09 codim-2 interbraid sandbox. Geometric counterexample only: two 4D balls are **not** an H(s)H worldtube B3 cross-section.

## Exact construction (all coordinates in length units)
In Euclidean R4, take equal closed 4-balls of radius R, centers c±=(0,0,0,±d/2), with 0<d<2R. Define length-valued constraints
F±(x)=(|x−c±|²−R²)/(2R).
The common zero set D={x4=0, x1²+x2²+x3²=r0²}, r0=√(R²−d²/4), is a closed S².

At (r0,0,0,0), the transverse normal Jacobian is
J=[[r0/R,−d/(2R)],[r0/R,+d/(2R)]].
Singular values √2 r0/R and d/(√2 R) give
**κ₂(J)=max(2r0/d,d/(2r0))**.
Optimal conditioning κ₂=1 occurs at d=√2 R; degeneracy occurs as d→0 or d→2R.

For the meridian Cε(t)=(r0+ε cos t,0,0,ε sin t), the constraint image is exactly
F±(Cε)=[εr0 cos t ∓(dε/2)sin t+ε²/2]/R.
The image is an ellipse centered at (ε²/2R,ε²/2R), with winding W=+1 for 0<ε<2r0, W undefined at ε=2r0 (contact), and W=0 beyond. Reversing orientation changes the sign.
For each ball **min F±=ε²/(2R)−ε**; for ε<R the winding-one meridian penetrates each filled ball by maximum radial depth ε.

## Exterior no-go (exact, not just numerical)
For impenetrable closed balls, every admissible exterior loop has F+>0 and F−>0 everywhere. Its constraint image is contained in the contractible positive quadrant, so
**W=(1/2π)∮(F+ dF−−F− dF+)/(F+²+F−²)=0**.
A closed S² boundary intersection does *not* itself create protected winding in the accessible exterior. A permeable/independently instantiated defect may have different admissibility, but requires physical construction.

## Numerical tests
Independent NumPy/SciPy solver, R=1, ε=.1, 16,384 intervals:
d/R | r0/R | κ₂ | W | min F±/R
0.2 | .994987 | 9.949874 | 1.000000 | −.095
0.5 | .968246 | 3.872983 | 1.000000 | −.095
1.0 | .866025 | 1.732051 | 1.000000 | −.095
√2 | .707107 | 1.000000 | 1.000000 | −.095
1.8 | .435890 | 2.064742 | 1.000000 | −.095
1.98 | .141067 | 7.017924 | 1.000000 | −.095

Negative controls: a fully exterior loop has min(F±)=.236477 and W≈5.1e−16; a large ε=1.5 meridian has W≈−6.4e−16. SO(4) rotation preserves F to 4.45e−16; N=32,64,256,2048,16384 all give W=1 within 1e−12. Direct/analytic F discrepancy <2.7e−16.

## Reproducible minimal algorithm
```python
import numpy as np
R=1.; d=np.sqrt(2); eps=.1; r=np.sqrt(R*R-d*d/4)
t=np.linspace(0,2*np.pi,16385)
x=np.stack([r+eps*np.cos(t),0*t,0*t,eps*np.sin(t)],axis=1)
centers=np.array([[0,0,0,d/2],[0,0,0,-d/2]])
F=np.sum((x[:,None,:]-centers)**2,axis=-1)/(2*R)-R/2
z=F[:,0]+1j*F[:,1]
W=np.angle(z[1:]/z[:-1]).sum()/(2*np.pi)
assert abs(W-1)<1e-12 and F.min()<0
```
